historical_reviews.v3_1: Collection coverage establishes the complete advertised option set and its member links; it is distinct from validating one BootOption member.

original_test_intent: Read the selected ComputerSystem BootOptions collection and validate its complete advertised option membership as a bounded read-only inventory snapshot.
original_method: Resolve the intended System and its BootOptions link, then use trusted curl/jq to GET the collection, validate collection identity/count/Members/pagination and retain approved redacted option-link metadata.
manual_activity: Provision the reusable secure Redfish access package and approved BootOptions collection schema/redaction policy; no per-run confirmation or manual boot action is required afterward.
required_inputs: BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Validated BootOptions link and collection schema
safety_requirements: Do not accept null `.BootOptions` output as evidence
Bound pagination and reject repeated links
No PATCH/POST boot changes, one-time boot, reboot, power or log clearing
agent_execution_scope: Resolve System and advertised BootOptions link
GET the collection under hard bounds
Capture status/headers and access-controlled raw hash
Validate collection identity, Members@odata.count, member links, uniqueness and pagination
engineer_actions: Maintain member-selection, schema and redaction policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: curl/jq are correct tools, but the fixed `system` ID is unverified and `.BootOptions` does not validate the collection's `Members`; a null filter result can look error-free.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With trusted TLS and secret-safe credentials, follow the selected System's advertised BootOptions link, require 2xx Redfish JSON, validate collection `@odata.id`, count, unique member links and bounded pagination, and export only approved metadata.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The BootOptions collection GET and 15/10 timing remain; no SystemId, option count or member IDs are inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a schema-aware collection validator that follows the advertised BootOptions link, verifies complete bounded membership and leaves boot settings unchanged.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces fixed member identity, hardcoded credentials/TLS bypass and a null-prone jq field with link, collection and pagination validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Adds collection completeness and member-link integrity; detailed validation of each option belongs to the separate BootOptionId case.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Device paths and option names can disclose platform topology, and collections may be empty or paginated by design; expected population policy must distinguish supported empty state from collection failure.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish SDK is equivalent if it preserves the selected System/BootOptions link, certificate binding, collection count/Members and pagination evidence. Reading a single BootOption does not satisfy collection completeness.
expected_evidence: Immutable BMC and selected System identity
Validated System→BootOptions link and firmware/schema version
HTTP status/content type and raw response hash
Collection identity, count, unique Members and pagination audit
Redacted option-link metadata and tool versions
No boot write, reboot, power, firmware or log mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master item and URI consistently describe the BootOptions collection. DeepSeek's fixed SystemId and incorrect jq projection are generated-review defects, not contradictions within the Master source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The collection operation and parent resource are explicit and can run after standard secure access, link-resolution and schema configuration.

review_improvement: Changes a null-prone guessed query into a complete, bounded and identity-bound BootOptions collection validation distinct from member-level coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BootOptions endpoint is a Redfish collection whose useful evidence is its identity, member count, unique `Members` links and pagination behavior. Filtering `.BootOptions` assumes a wrapper property that may not exist and can silently produce null. The collector must derive the URI from the selected System, enforce termination and preserve the full member-link set so missing, duplicate or cross-System options cannot be hidden by a human-readable response.
